albums.title: Melody A.M.
albums.reason: With 1062 all-time plays, Röyksopp are one of your deepest loves — and this debut is where it all began, a glacial, beautiful record you may not have sat with properly in years.

albums.title: Orbital (The Brown Album)
albums.reason: Orbital have 777 all-time plays and tracks like 'Don't Stop Me' in your top 50 — this is the raw, thrilling record that launched them, and it deserves a revisit from the start.

albums.title: Angles
albums.reason: You've given The Strokes 659 all-time plays and their first three albums were already recommended — Angles is the overlooked fourth chapter, full of the same downtown energy with a stranger, more experimental edge.

albums.title: Play
albums.reason: Moby sits at 551 all-time plays and 'Porcelain' is deep in your history — Play is the defining statement, threading blues samples through electronic beds in a way that still sounds unlike anything else.

albums.title: Exit Planet Dust
albums.reason: 556 all-time plays for The Chemical Brothers tells the story — this debut is where they invented their sound, and it predates most of what you've been recommended from them so far.

albums.title: Echo Park
albums.reason: Feeder have 768 all-time plays and 'Buck Rogers' is one of your most-played tracks — Echo Park is the album that track lives on, a perfectly crafted British rock record from an era you clearly cherished.

albums.title: Harbour
albums.reason: Trentemøller has 560 all-time plays and five of his albums have been recommended, but Harbour — his most recent and most hushed — is still untouched and fits the recent-vault window perfectly.

albums.title: Immunity
albums.reason: Jon Hopkins tracks are deep in your recent history and Singularity was already recommended — Immunity is the breakthrough album, moving from glacial ambience into full dancefloor transcendence across a single arc.

albums.title: Late Night Tales: Bonobo
albums.reason: You've given Bonobo enormous play across recent years, and every studio album has been recommended — this stunning mix compilation from 2013 is a legitimate gap, showing the records and sounds that shaped him.

albums.title: Hallowed
albums.reason: Maribou State have 434 all-time plays and every earlier album was already recommended — Hallowed is their newest and most confident record, and it sounds like a natural next chapter from Kingdoms in Colour.

albums.title: Playing Robots into Heaven
albums.reason: James Blake has 637 all-time plays and five of his albums were already recommended — Playing Robots into Heaven is his most recent and most danceable record, a genuine surprise that strips everything back to pure electronic joy.

albums.title: The North Borders Remixed
albums.reason: You've been deep in Bonobo across the recent vault era and every studio album is covered — this official remix collection reframes The North Borders material through the lens of artists like Machinedrum and Totally Enormous Extinct Dinosaurs, keeping it fresh and untouched in your history.

albums.title: R.I.P.
albums.reason: Your love of Aphex Twin, Orbital, and Plaid points straight at Actress — R.I.P. is his masterpiece, a corroded, emotionally strange record that sits at the intersection of techno, ambient, and something entirely its own.

albums.title: Mutant
albums.reason: Your taste in Aphex Twin and Justice's harder edges suggests Arca would hit hard — Mutant is visceral and bizarre, a record that pushes club music into genuinely unsettling emotional territory.

albums.title: Velocity : Design : Comfort
albums.reason: Your deep love of Daft Punk, Moby, and Air points toward this cult classic — a blissed-out fusion of shoegaze and IDM that sounds like Discovery's more introverted twin and remains criminally overlooked.

albums.title: Alpinisms
albums.reason: If you love The Shins' melodic instinct and Massive Attack's atmospheric density, School of Seven Bells' debut will feel like a revelation — layered, euphoric, and deeply emotional.

albums.title: Nostalchic
albums.reason: Your affection for James Blake and Bonobo's textural approach makes Lapalux a natural discovery — Nostalchic is warm, melancholic, and constructed with the same emotional precision you clearly respond to.

albums.title: Stainless Style
albums.reason: Your love of Gorillaz, MGMT, and Justice's playful maximalism points here — this Super Furry Animals side project is a gloriously trashy, melodically irresistible concept album about car magnate John DeLorean.

albums.title: Phase
albums.reason: Your recent immersion in Khruangbin, St Germain, and the Oscar Peterson Trio suggests Mildlife would land perfectly — this Melbourne group blends motorik krautrock with jazz and deep funk in a way that feels completely of your current arc.

albums.title: Onwards to the Permanent Gold
albums.reason: You've played Alabaster DePlume 52 times this year and explored most of his catalogue — this 2021 album is a genuine gap, a warm and urgent record that shares the same tender, human spirit you keep returning to.

albums.title: The Imperfect Sea
albums.reason: Your recent listens to Nils Frahm, Ólafur Arnalds, and A Winged Victory for the Sullen point directly at Penguin Cafe — this album is warm, unhurried, and beautifully constructed from strings, piano, and found sound.

albums.title: Night Melody
albums.reason: Rival Consoles' Overflow and Persona are already recommended but Night Melody (2024) is untouched — and given your love of Ben Lukas Boysen, Nils Frahm, and Max Cooper, this focused, melodic new record is an ideal discovery.

albums.title: Everything Ablaze
albums.reason: Your heavy rotation of Nils Frahm, Hania Rani, and Joep Beving this year positions you perfectly for Hior Chronik — a Greek composer whose sparse, luminous piano work lives in the same quiet emotional space.

albums.title: Fragments
albums.reason: You've been deep in Bonobo all week — Cirrus, Kong, Drift — and Fragments is the album that bridges his most meditative and most danceable impulses, which is exactly where your listening seems to be right now.

albums.title: U.F.Orb
albums.reason: You played The Orb's 'Golden Clouds' this week, and U.F.Orb is the deep vault that track belongs to — a hypnotic, sprawling ambient house classic that rewards exactly the kind of loose, immersive listening you're in right now.

albums.title: Screamadelica
albums.reason: You played Primal Scream four times in the last month — Screamadelica is the defining statement, a record that dissolves the line between rock, rave, and gospel into something genuinely transcendent.

albums.title: Live at Capitol Studios
albums.reason: You've been playing Khruangbin heavily this week and every studio album has already come up — this intimate live session captures exactly the warm, unhurried groove you're clearly in right now, stripped back to just the trio.

albums.title: Beaucoup Fish
albums.reason: Underworld appeared in your last-month plays and you have 636 all-time plays for them — Beaucoup Fish sits between their two greatest albums and contains some of their most muscular, euphoric dance music, perfect for the energy you seem to be chasing.

albums.title: The Universe Smiles Upon You
albums.reason: You've been deep in Khruangbin all week and this debut is the untouched origin point — the same warm, bass-heavy, globe-trotting groove you're clearly in right now, just at its most stripped-back and unhurried.

songs.title: Shine On You Crazy Diamond (Parts I-V)
songs.reason: Pink Floyd have 1199 all-time plays and their major albums were already recommended — this nine-minute opening suite from Wish You Were Here is one of the most emotionally sustained pieces they ever recorded, and it deserves a full, unhurried sit.

songs.title: Safe from Harm
songs.reason: 534 all-time plays for Massive Attack and their albums are covered — 'Safe from Harm' is the opening track from Blue Lines that set the entire trip-hop blueprint, a moment of pure tension and release that holds up perfectly.

songs.title: Champagne Supernova
songs.reason: Oasis have 617 all-time plays and sit solidly in the deep-vault era — this slow-burning, six-minute closer from (What's the Story) Morning Glory? is one of the grandest things they ever recorded and a perfect nostalgic return.

songs.title: Rez
songs.reason: Your 636 all-time Underworld plays go deep and tracks like 'Born Slippy' are covered — 'Rez' is the relentless, ascending rave anthem that defines a certain euphoric feeling and may not have had a spin in years.

songs.title: A Day in the Life
songs.reason: 831 all-time plays for The Beatles and 'While My Guitar Gently Weeps' is already recommended — 'A Day in the Life' is the closing masterpiece of Sgt. Pepper's, arguably the greatest song they ever made, worth returning to with fresh ears.

songs.title: Runaway
songs.reason: 623 all-time Kanye plays puts him deep in your vault — 'Runaway' is a nine-minute requiem for ego and self-destruction from My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy, one of the most emotionally naked moments in his catalogue.

songs.title: Eating Hooks
songs.reason: Your all-time play count for Moderat is significant and 'Rusty Nails' was already recommended — 'Eating Hooks' from the II album is the hushed, devastatingly sad counterpart, a track that hits harder the more you let it breathe.

songs.title: Open Eye Signal
songs.reason: Jon Hopkins tracks have appeared in your recent data and 'Emerald Rush' was already recommended — 'Open Eye Signal' is the nine-minute centrepiece of Immunity, the definitive statement of his dancefloor-as-cathedral approach.

songs.title: Hollow
songs.reason: Rival Consoles appear in your recent data and other tracks have been recommended — 'Hollow' from Persona is an undulating, luminous piece of modular synthesis that shares the emotional architecture of your Ben Lukas Boysen and Nils Frahm listening.

songs.title: Steal
songs.reason: 434 all-time Maribou State plays and several of their tracks have already been recommended — 'Steal' from Kingdoms in Colour is a quietly devastating, groove-anchored track that deserves more attention in your rotation.

songs.title: Jupiters
songs.reason: Four Tet appears in your recent 12-month data and several tracks were already recommended — 'Jupiters' from New Energy is the exhilarating peak of that album, a rush of warmth and rhythm that sits perfectly in your recent-vault era.

songs.title: Papillon
songs.reason: With 434 all-time Maribou State plays and several tracks already surfaced, 'Papillon' from their Kingdoms in Colour era is an untouched gem — a gently euphoric, slow-building piece that captures the emotional warmth you keep returning to in their catalogue.

songs.title: Be Rude to Your School
songs.reason: Your deep love of Plaid, Aphex Twin, and Boards of Canada points directly at Plone — this Warp Records gem is full of childlike, melodically irresistible electronic tunes that feel like a lost cousin to everything you love from that era.

songs.title: Myam James Part 1
songs.reason: Your deep love of Plaid, Aphex Twin, and Röyksopp points straight at Kettel — a Dutch producer whose warm, melodically generous IDM sits in exactly the same emotional register, and this track is one of his most beloved.

songs.title: Needle & Thread
songs.reason: Your love of Leftfield, Orbital, and Underworld's more muscular moments suggests Objekt's surgical, deeply rhythmic approach would resonate — 'Needle & Thread' is his most hypnotic and accomplished piece of UK club engineering.

songs.title: Ghosst(s)
songs.reason: Your affection for Rone, Trentemøller, and the darker shades of Justice points at Lorn — 'Ghosst(s)' is a shadow-drenched, slow-burning centrepiece from his Ask the Dust debut, full of dread and strange beauty.

songs.title: Lost Where I Belong
songs.reason: Your love of James Blake, Massive Attack's vocal moments, and Stevie Wonder's emotional directness suggests Andreya Triana — this track is a stunning piece of electronic soul, produced by Bonobo, that sits in a space you clearly love.

songs.title: Radar
songs.reason: Your deep love of Plaid, Aphex Twin, and the more melodic end of electronic music points at Hauschka — a Düsseldorf composer who uses prepared piano and electronic loops to build music that's genuinely joyful and rhythmically irresistible.

songs.title: Who Are You?
songs.reason: Your recent love of Portico Quartet, the Oscar Peterson Trio, and Ill Considered points at Joel Ross — a young vibraphonist whose warm, searching jazz has exactly the emotional openness and rhythmic intelligence you've been drawn to.

songs.title: Snaxx
songs.reason: Your recent immersion in Khruangbin, Erykah Badu, and the looser end of soul and jazz points at Mndsgn — Snaxx is a blissed-out, sun-faded record of soft funk and bedroom R&B that matches your current unhurried, warm listening arc.

songs.title: Svalbard
songs.reason: Your heavy rotation of Nils Frahm, Hania Rani, and Ben Lukas Boysen this year makes Niklas Paschburg an obvious next discovery — this debut is cinematic, quietly devastating Nordic piano music with electronic undercurrents that feel perfectly calibrated to your current mood.

songs.title: It Makes You Forget (Itgehane)
songs.reason: Your recent plays of COEO, Super Flu, and DJ Koze point directly at Peggy Gou's warm, endlessly looping minimal house — this track is one of the most purely pleasurable pieces of underground dance music from recent years.

songs.title: Lavender & Red Beans
songs.reason: Your deep recent engagement with Bill Withers, Syl Johnson, and Charles Bradley — that warm, emotionally direct strand of soul — points directly at Meshell Ndegeocello, whose bass-anchored, quietly radical soul music inhabits exactly the same dignified, unhurried space.

songs.title: Tides
songs.reason: You've been deep in Bonobo all week across multiple albums — 'Tides' from Black Sands is one of his most hypnotic and sustained pieces, a slow-building trip-hop meditation that fits the mood of your current listening perfectly.

songs.title: Little Fluffy Clouds
songs.reason: You played The Orb this week and their classic early material is where it all began — 'Little Fluffy Clouds' is a piece of genuinely euphoric, deeply strange ambient house that still sounds unlike almost anything else.

songs.title: Loaded
songs.reason: Primal Scream had four plays in your last month and Screamadelica is the album pick — 'Loaded' is the seven-minute opening statement that fused rock with rave culture and changed what both could sound like.

songs.title: Time (You and I)
songs.reason: You've been playing Khruangbin heavily this week and this track from Mordechai — with its soft, unhurried groove and warm vocal drift — matches the relaxed, immersive energy of your current listening exactly.

songs.title: Theory of Colours
songs.reason: You played Dauwd's 'Lydia' this week and that track lives on his debut album Theory of Colours — a quiet, luminous record of miniature electronic pieces that shares the introspective, warm quality running through your recent plays.

songs.title: Simple Things
songs.reason: You played Pat Lok's 'Might Be on Fire' most recently of all your tracks this week — 'Simple Things' is one of his warmest and most accomplished pieces, a soulful, groove-anchored production that extends the same late-night, feel-good energy you're clearly in.
